components.css: .ds-root{--g:#121c18;--p:#172420;--r:#1d2d28;--rule:#2f4a40;--t:#e9e4d4;--m:#a8b0a4;--a:#c8623a;--at:#e07a50;--oa:#0b120f;background:var(--g);color:var(--t);padding:16px;font-family:Barlow,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-opts{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;border-top:1px solid var(--rule)}.ds-opts li{border-bottom:1px solid var(--rule)}.ds-opt{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:16px;width:100%;background:transparent;border:0;color:var(--t);font:400 20px/1.35 Barlow,sans-serif;min-height:56px;padding:8px 16px;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 120ms,border-color 120ms}.ds-opt:hover{background:var(--r)}.ds-opt:hover .ds-kbd{border-color:var(--a)}.ds-opt:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--t);outline-offset:-2px}.ds-opt .ds-kbd{font-size:.75em;height:1.8em;min-width:1.8em}.ds-kbd{display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;min-width:34px;height:34px;border:1px solid var(--rule);border-radius:2px;color:var(--m);font:600 16px/1 'Barlow Condensed',sans-serif;letter-spacing:.06em;padding:0 6px}

components.css: .ds-root{--g:#121c18;--p:#172420;--r:#1d2d28;--rule:#2f4a40;--t:#e9e4d4;--m:#a8b0a4;--a:#c8623a;--at:#e07a50;--oa:#0b120f;background:var(--g);color:var(--t);padding:16px;font-family:Barlow,system-ui,sans-serif}.ds-line{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0}.ds-line li{position:relative;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;min-height:40px;padding-left:20px;color:var(--m);font-size:15px}.ds-line li::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:3px;top:0;height:100%;border-left:1px solid var(--rule)}.ds-line li.e::before{border-left-style:dashed;height:50%}.ds-line li span{position:absolute;left:0;width:8px;height:8px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--m)}.ds-line li.c span{background:var(--a)}.ds-line li.e span{background:var(--g);border:1px solid var(--m)}

narrative.overview: Pattern Drill looks like the laminated card a pilot clips to a yoke: ruled boxes, one active step, a station line that records where you have been. Every surface is flat, hairline-ruled and solid. The only warm thing on screen is the step you are on and the action that moves you forward.
keyCharacteristics: Flat, ruled, solid: 1px rules and tonal panels instead of shadows.
One rust accent, used for the current step and the primary action only.
Condensed caps for titles and labels, Barlow for body, Fira Code for code only.
Digits live in fixed cells and never reflow.
Keyboard-first: every control shows or implies its key.

rules.name: The One Voice Rule
rules.body: Rust marks the current step and the primary action. If two rust things compete on one screen, one of them is wrong.

rules.name: The Two-Token Rule
rules.body: Large fills use Field Rust; small text uses Lit Rust. Do not swap them.

rules.name: The Syntax Ground Rule
rules.body: Highlighted code always sits on Code Well, in both themes. Never put the syntax palette on a light surface.

rules.name: The Caps-For-Names Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a thing (titles, labels, buttons) is condensed caps with tracking. Anything that explains a thing is Barlow in sentence case.

rules.name: The Rem Rule
rules.body: Sizes that carry text are rem or derived from rem, so layouts survive a larger root font.

rules.name: The Flat-Always Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, backdrop-filter, gradient or glow, at rest or on hover. If something needs to stand forward, raise its tone one step.

dos: Do use only the --pd-* tokens for new surfaces; legacy variables exist for Reference and resolve to them.
Do give every new control a visible key hint or an aria-keyshortcuts value, matching the Finder's key-cap pattern.
Do keep digits in fixed-width cells and give changing numbers a fixed box.
Do show state with colour and border only, and keep transitions to 120ms.
Do derive heights that wrap text from rem, not px, so a larger root font cannot clip descenders.
Do keep focus rings at 2px Bone, offset 2px, on every interactive element.
donts: Don't add shadows, blur, glass, gradients, glows or decorative background images.
Don't use rust for anything other than the current step, the primary action and the selection highlight.
Don't use Field Rust as small text on dark; use Lit Rust.
Don't round anything beyond 2px, or use pills.
Don't enforce the clock. Overtime is shown in Coral and the run continues.
Don't center the Finder in a floating quiz card, or replace the station line with a progress bar.
Don't put highlighted code on a light surface.
